name: Familial Paroxysmal Exercise-Induced Dystonia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Paroxysmal Exercise-Induced Dystonia

criteria.description: Recurrent episodes of dystonia triggered specifically by prolonged exercise
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Normal neurological examination between dystonic episodes
Exclusion of secondary causes of dystonia and other paroxysmal movement disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent exercise-induced dystonia episodes plus positive family history and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for mutations in the SLC2A1 gene may support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically affects lower limbs during or immediately after prolonged exercise

pathognomonic.symptomName: Transient dystonia episodes lasting minutes to hours

occasional.symptomName: Mild anxiety related to exercise avoidance

laboratory: Possible low cerebrospinal fluid glucose during episodes
genetic: Mutations in SLC2A1 gene (GLUT1 deficiency syndrome) in some familial cases
other: Electromyography during episodes may show dystonic muscle activity

distinguishingFeatures: Episodes triggered by sudden movement rather than prolonged exercise
Shorter duration of attacks (seconds to minutes)
Responds well to anticonvulsants like carbamazepine
Onset in childhood with diurnal fluctuation

redFlags: Lack of family history in suspected cases
references: Klein C, Fahn S. Paroxysmal dyskinesias. In: Bradley’s Neurology in Clinical Practice. 7th ed. 2016.
Wang D, et al. Familial paroxysmal exercise-induced dystonia and GLUT1 deficiency. Neurology. 2011;77(3):280-286.
